## R293 — migrate grok xychart_diagram.rs -> render_xychart_diagram_to_svg (direction (1) brick 24: 15th per-diagram leaf, 14th self-contained SVG emitter)

Anchor:R293-1 <pending>

### Round goal

Port grok ``xychart_diagram.rs`` (867 lines) to Python ``render_xychart_diagram_to_svg`` as a functional clone (not a line-by-line transcription), wiring it into the ``render.py`` dispatch so an ``xychart-beta`` mermaid source renders to a self-contained SVG string. This is the 24th brick of direction (1) (activate dagre: mermaid end-to-end rendering), the 15th per-diagram leaf, and the 14th self-contained SVG emitter -- same lineage as R279 info / R281 radar / R282 pie / R283 packet / R284 sankey / R285 gantt / R286 kanban / R287 timeline / R288 quadrant / R289 block / R290 journey / R291 gitgraph / R292 mindmap.

### Fusion conclusion

Xychart is the family's first cartesian-axis chart (a line series plotted against d3-generated "nice" tick axes on a fixed 700x500 canvas), and like R292 mindmap it bypasses the R268 dagre layout engine entirely -- the axes are computed from the data range via the d3_ticks "nice number" algorithm, not laid out by a rank/position pass. Two load-bearing clone details shape the port. First, the SVG root's attribute order (grok L95): ``id="my-svg"`` is emitted as the LAST attribute, after ``width="100%"`` -- not as the first attribute after ``<svg ``. This byte-order fidelity matters because the dispatch-smoke test must NOT anchor on ``<svg id="my-svg"``; the initial test draft did exactly that and failed, and the fix was to relax the assertion to a non-anchored substring ``'id="my-svg"' in svg`` after grep-verifying grok L95. Second, the axis-title groups are CONDITIONAL: ``<g class="x-axis-title">`` fires only ``if chart.x_title`` and ``<g class="y-axis-title">`` fires only ``if chart.y_title`` (grok ``if !chart.x_title.is_empty()`` / ``if !chart.y_title.is_empty()``). The y-axis directive ``y-axis "Sales" 0 --> 100`` simultaneously sets BOTH the label and the range (grok ``parse_y_axis`` returns ``(String, Option<(f64,f64)>)``), while a bare ``y-axis 0 --> 100`` sets an EMPTY y_title and thus does NOT fire the y-axis-title group. The initial ``_CATEGORY_CHART`` fixture used the bare form and the ``test_y_axis_title_uses_rotate_minus_90`` test failed (group absent); the fix was to give the fixture a labeled range (``y-axis "Sales" 0 --> 100``), not to weaken the implementation. Both fixes continue R292's "implementation-is-source-of-truth" discipline: when implementation (mirroring grok) and test disagree, grep the grok source and correct the test. The functional contract cloned: the ``xychart-beta`` header + ``title``/``x-axis``/``y-axis``/``line`` directives, the d3_ticks "nice number" tick generator (``_round`` half-away-from-zero to align ticks to round integers, ``_scale_linear`` mapping data->pixel, ``_format_tick``/``_fmt`` rendering), the fixed 700x500 canvas (``CHART_WIDTH``/``CHART_HEIGHT``), the Tableau-10 series palette (NOT theme-derived), the 2-channel theme binding (``text_color`` -> axis stroke + text fill; ``background`` -> SVG root style + main-group background rect), the conditional axis-title groups, and the ``&#39;`` numeric-entity escape variant.

### Evidence

1. **fixed-canvas cartesian layout bypasses dagre (the family's second non-dagre layout after R292 mindmap)** -- xychart plots line series against d3-generated axes on a fixed ``CHART_WIDTH=700`` x ``CHART_HEIGHT=500`` canvas. The y-range resolves from the data (auto-range) or from an explicit ``y-axis L --> H`` directive; the x-axis is a categorical band (``x-axis "Month" [Jan, Feb, Mar]``). Tick positions come from the d3_ticks "nice number" algorithm (``_d3_ticks``), which picks a tick count near the requested density and snaps each tick to a "nice" value via ``_round`` (half-away-from-zero so 0.5 -> 1, not 0). Pixel coordinates are computed by ``_scale_linear`` (linear interpolation domain->range). The port carries this verbatim; forcing xychart through dagre would lose the axis semantics (categorical bands, nice ticks).
2. **SVG root ``id="my-svg"`` is the LAST attribute (grok L95, the load-bearing byte-order detail)** -- grok emits the root as ``<svg aria-roledescription="xychart" role="graphics-document document" viewBox="0 0 {W} {H}" style="max-width: {W}px; background-color: {bg};" xmlns="..." xmlns:xlink="..." width="100%" id="my-svg">``. Note ``id="my-svg"`` comes AFTER ``width="100%"``, not first. The initial dispatch-smoke test asserted ``'<svg id="my-svg"' in svg`` (anchored) and failed; grep-verification of grok L95 confirmed the order, so the test was relaxed to ``'id="my-svg"' in svg`` (non-anchored substring), mirroring ``test_svg_carries_my_svg_id_and_xychart_role``. This byte-order fidelity is the R293 analog of R292's n_children==0 early return: an implementation detail that looks incidental but is grok's actual emission, so the test adapts.
3. **d3_ticks "nice number" algorithm (``_round`` half-away-from-zero)** -- the tick generator mirrors d3's ``ticks``/``nice`` pair: given a domain ``[min, max]`` and a target count, it derives a step from the ``10^floor(log10(range/count))`` family, rounds the step to 1/2/5 x 10^k, then snaps each tick to a "nice" multiple. ``_round`` uses half-away-from-zero (Python's built-in ``round`` is banker's rounding, so ``_round(0.5)`` must give ``1``, not ``0``) -- a subtle port detail where a naive ``round()`` would diverge from grok's f64 rounding on .5 boundaries. ``_format_tick``/``_fmt`` render the tick value (dropping the trailing ``.0`` for integer-valued floats, mirroring Rust's f64 Display).
4. **2-channel theme binding + Tableau-10 series palette (NON-theme)** -- xychart binds exactly 2 theme channels: ``text_color`` flows into the axis stroke and the axis text fill; ``background`` flows into the SVG root ``style="background-color: {bg};"`` and the main-group background ``<rect>``. The series colors come from the hard-coded Tableau-10 palette (``SERIES_PALETTE = ("#4e79a7", "#f28e2b", "#e15759", "#76b7b2", "#59a14f", "#edc948", "#b07aa1", "#ff9da7", "#9c755f", "#bab0ac")``), cycled ``series_index % 10`` -- NOT from the resolved ``MermaidTheme``. This places xychart at the 2-channel tier of the family's theme-awareness spectrum, above R290/R292 (0 channels) and below R289 block (5 channels). "Clone by function" demands this be ported faithfully -- deriving series colors from theme would diverge from grok.
5. **conditional axis-title groups + y-axis labeled-range parsing (grok L210-220, L284-286, L350)** -- the ``<g class="x-axis-title">`` group fires only ``if chart.x_title`` and ``<g class="y-axis-title">`` fires only ``if chart.y_title`` (grok ``if !chart.x_title.is_empty()``). The y-axis directive has two forms: a LABELED range ``y-axis "Sales" 0 --> 100`` sets BOTH ``chart.y_title`` and the y-range (grok ``parse_y_axis`` returns ``(label, Some((lo, hi)))``), while a bare range ``y-axis 0 --> 100`` sets ``y_title`` to an EMPTY string (``parse_y_axis`` returns ``("", Some((lo, hi)))``) and thus does NOT fire the y-axis-title group. The initial ``_CATEGORY_CHART`` fixture used the bare form; ``test_y_axis_title_uses_rotate_minus_90`` failed (group absent); the fix was to give the fixture a labeled range (``y-axis "Sales" 0 --> 100``), confirmed safe because the three tests sharing ``_CATEGORY_CHART`` assert only group-class presence, never coordinate values.
6. **escape_xml ``&#39;`` numeric-entity variant + ``axisl-line`` spelling (byte-alignment fidelity)** -- xychart escapes ``'`` as ``&#39;`` (numeric entity), NOT ``&apos;`` (named entity). This is a deliberate divergence from R290 journey / R289 block / R291 gitgraph, which all use ``&apos;``. The two variants coexist in the family because grok's renderers were authored independently; "clone by function" preserves each renderer's actual emission rather than "unifying" them. Similarly, the axis-line group class is spelled ``axisl-line`` (grok L169), NOT ``axis-line`` -- a grok typo that the port carries verbatim for byte-alignment fidelity (the test asserts ``'class="axisl-line"'``).
7. **dispatch wiring + bucket-guard sync + barrel unchanged + clean feat (2 ruff B905 fixes pre-feat)** -- ``render.py`` gains ``if diagram_type == "xychart-beta": return render_xychart_diagram_to_svg(body, resolved_theme)`` and ``"xychart-beta"`` is removed from ``_UNSUPPORTED_DIAGRAM_TYPES`` (10 -> 9 tokens). R291 gitgraph's test and R292 mindmap's test BOTH encoded ``len(_UNSUPPORTED_DIAGRAM_TYPES) == 10``; R293's removal of ``xychart-beta`` (10 -> 9) breaks both assertions -- a bucket-guard sync updates each test to ``== 9`` with a docstring noting R293's subsequent shrinkage. This is the explicit, documented exception to the "do not break iteration independence" rule (established R282, continued R283-R292). The feat commit spans 6 files (the family's widest yet): the xychart renderer + render dispatch + xychart tests + render tests (parametrize xychart-beta removed + 4 docstrings) + gitgraph test sync + mindmap test sync. The barrel ``to_svg/__all__`` stays 18 (R277 baseline) -- xychart is reached only via the dispatch arm. Two ruff B905 fixes (``zip()`` missing ``strict=``) were applied to ``xychart_diagram.py`` BEFORE the feat commit (L797 x-axis label loop + L832 y-axis label loop), both with ``strict=False`` mirroring grok's Rust ``zip`` (takes the shorter iterator; the two lists are co-generated by ``_layout_x_axis`` / the y-tick generator and are always equal-length). The feat therefore landed clean: ruff ``All checks passed!`` and full mermaid green at commit time.

## R294 — migrate grok requirement_diagram.rs -> render_requirement_diagram_to_svg (direction (1) brick 25: 16th per-diagram leaf, 15th self-contained SVG emitter, FIRST dagre-consuming renderer)

Anchor:R294-1 <pending>

### Round goal

Port grok ``requirement_diagram.rs`` (874 lines) to Python ``render_requirement_diagram_to_svg`` as a functional clone (not a line-by-line transcription), wiring it into the ``render.py`` dispatch so a ``requirementDiagram`` mermaid source renders to a self-contained SVG string. This is the 25th brick of direction (1) (activate dagre: mermaid end-to-end rendering), the 16th per-diagram leaf, and the 15th self-contained SVG emitter. **It is also the family's FIRST renderer to actually consume the dagre layout engine** -- a lineage milestone. R279 info / R281 radar / R282 pie / R283 packet / R284 sankey / R285 gantt / R286 kanban / R287 timeline / R288 quadrant / R289 block / R290 journey / R291 gitgraph / R292 mindmap / R293 xychart all emit bespoke geometry; ``requirementDiagram`` delegates node placement and edge routing to the R246-R268 dagre stack (rank/order/position), then reads back the computed coordinates. The dagre engine that direction (1) spent 22 bricks building finally has a paying customer.

### Fusion conclusion

requirementDiagram is the renderer that proves the dagre investment. Unlike R292 mindmap ( bespoke tree layout) and R293 xychart (bespoke cartesian axes), it builds a ``minimax_code.data_structures.Graph`` with ``GraphOption(directed=True, multigraph=True, compound=False)``, hands it to ``dagre_layout``, and consumes the returned node boxes + edge waypoints to emit SVG ``<g>`` groups and ``<path>`` elements. Three load-bearing clone details shape the port. First, **``compound=False`` is deliberate**: requirement diagrams carry no subgraphs, so the graph is built non-compound; this sidesteps the pre-existing ``network_simplex._exchange_edges`` defect (``None -= 1`` on intra-subgraph chained edges, the ``long_identifier`` xfail(strict=True)) by keeping dagre on the plain simplex branch. Second, **forward/backward ``contains`` semantics are asymmetric (the core grok behavior)**: a forward edge ``A -contains-> B`` parses to ``rel_type == "-contains"`` (the leading dash survives because ``-contains`` is not the bare ``-`` token), so ``is_contains = (rel_type == "contains")`` is False -> the edge renders DASHED (``stroke-dasharray: 10,7``) WITH an arrowEnd marker; a backward edge ``A <- contains - B`` parses with the standalone ``-`` filtered out, leaving ``rel_type == "contains"`` (no dash) -> ``is_contains`` is True -> the edge renders SOLID with NO marker. The ``is_contains`` check at L858 is the single branch point; cloning grok's parse filter verbatim is what reproduces the asymmetry. Third, **the divider line carries a signature ``stroke-width="1.3"`` attribute** (L909, the divider line ONLY -- the style block uses CSS colon form ``stroke-width:1.3;`` and the marker crosshair ``<line>`` has no width attribute), so the test asserts divider presence by scoping to the node ``<g>`` and checking ``stroke-width="1.3"`` rather than a naive global ``"<line" in svg`` (which also matches marker crosshairs). The functional contract cloned: the ``requirementDiagram`` header + ``direction`` declaration + 7-kind node blocks (``element`` / ``requirement`` / ``functionalrequirement`` / ``interfacerequirement`` / ``performancerequirement`` / ``physicalrequirement`` / ``designconstraint``), the typed AST (``RequirementNode`` L114 with ``requirement_id`` + body props), the dagre-backed ``compute_requirement_box_layout`` (L626-L707), the 7-kind ``type_line`` map (``functionalrequirement`` -> ``"Functional Requirement"`` etc.), the 5-channel theme binding, and the asymmetric contains rendering.

### Evidence

1. **FIRST renderer to consume the dagre engine (the lineage milestone)** -- R279-R293 all emit bespoke geometry (tree/cartesian/polar/etc.) and bypass dagre entirely. ``requirementDiagram`` is the first per-diagram renderer to build a real ``Graph`` and call ``dagre_layout``: nodes are placed by the rank/order/position pipeline (R250-R268), edges are routed by the layout's edge-point computation, and the renderer reads back ``node.x``/``node.y``/``node.width``/``node.height`` plus edge waypoints to emit ``<g class="node default">`` boxes and ``<path>`` connectors. This validates the 22-brick dagre investment: the engine now has a paying customer in the renderer family.
2. **``compound=False`` sidesteps the pre-existing network_simplex defect (L528/L542)** -- the graph is built ``GraphOption(directed=True, multigraph=True, compound=False)`` because requirement diagrams carry no subgraphs. This is load-bearing: compound graphs route dagre through the ``network_simplex`` path that has the ``_exchange_edges`` ``None -= 1`` defect on intra-subgraph chained edges (the ``long_identifier`` xfail). By staying non-compound, ``requirementDiagram`` avoids triggering the defect while still exercising the full rank/order/position stack. When the dagre edge-swap fix lands, this renderer's behavior is unchanged (it never hit the defect), but the compound path opens up for future subgraph-carrying diagrams.
3. **forward/backward ``contains`` asymmetry -- the single ``is_contains`` branch (L858, core grok behavior)** -- ``is_contains = edge.rel_type == "contains"``. Forward ``A -contains-> B`` parses ``rel_type = "-contains"`` (the ``-contains`` token is not the bare ``-`` separator, so the leading dash is preserved) -> ``is_contains`` False -> ``dash = "stroke-dasharray: 10,7;"`` + arrowEnd marker. Backward ``A <- contains - B`` parses with the standalone ``-`` filtered out as a separator -> ``rel_type = "contains"`` (no leading dash) -> ``is_contains`` True -> ``dash = ""`` + NO marker. The ``id="A-B-0"`` (forward) vs ``id="B-A-0"`` (backward, src/dst flipped) edge ids are asserted in the suite. Cloning grok's separator filter verbatim is what reproduces the asymmetry; a "simpler" parser that stripped all dashes would collapse the two cases and diverge.
4. **5-channel theme-aware palette (the family's full-theme tier, alongside R289 block)** -- requirementDiagram binds 5 theme channels directly (NOT normalized): LIGHT ``background=#ffffff`` / ``text_color=#333333`` / ``edge_color=#333333`` / ``node_fill=#ECECFF`` / ``node_stroke=#9370DB``; DARK ``background=#1e1e1e`` / ``text_color=#ffffff`` / ``edge_color=#888888`` / ``node_fill=#2d2d2d`` / ``node_stroke=#888888``. The theme values render verbatim (no re-derivation). This places requirementDiagram at the 5-channel tier of the family's theme-awareness spectrum (above R293 xychart's 2 channels / R290-R292's 0 channels, level with R289 block). The public entry takes ``theme`` (not ``_theme``) and threads it into the dagre-fed emitter.
5. **7-kind node ``type_line`` map (grok kind enum)** -- nodes come in 7 kinds: ``element`` -> ``"<<Element>>"`` / ``requirement`` -> ``"<<Requirement>>"`` (also the fallback) / ``functionalrequirement`` -> ``"<<Functional Requirement>>"`` / ``interfacerequirement`` -> ``"<<Interface Requirement>>"`` / ``performancerequirement`` -> ``"<<Performance Requirement>>"`` / ``physicalrequirement`` -> ``"<<Physical Requirement>>"`` / ``designconstraint`` -> ``"<<Design Constraint>>"``. Grok parses the kind token lowercased-merged (``functionalrequirement``) and renders the guillemet-wrapped display form; the port carries both verbatim. The suite parametrizes all 7 kinds.
6. **divider line signature ``stroke-width="1.3"`` (attribute form, divider ONLY -- L909)** -- a node with a body (requirement/element with props) gets an internal divider ``<line>`` carrying the attribute ``stroke-width="1.3"`` (grok L909); a bare element node (``element System { }`` -- no body) emits NO divider. The signature is load-bearing for testing: a naive ``"<line" in svg`` assertion also matches the arrowEnd marker crosshair ``<line>`` elements, so the suite scopes to the node ``<g>`` group (``_node_group`` helper) and asserts ``stroke-width="1.3"`` presence/absence. Note the three coexisting ``stroke-width`` forms: divider attribute ``stroke-width="1.3"`` (this renderer's divider), style-block CSS ``stroke-width:1.3;`` (colon form), marker crosshair ``<line>`` (no width attribute) -- cloning by function preserves all three rather than "unifying" them.
7. **dispatch wiring + 3-way bucket-guard sync + barrel unchanged + clean feat (ruff zero-fix)** -- ``render.py`` gains ``if diagram_type == "requirementDiagram": return render_requirement_diagram_to_svg(body, resolved_theme)`` (L447-448) and ``"requirementDiagram"`` is removed from ``_UNSUPPORTED_DIAGRAM_TYPES`` (9 -> 8 tokens, L172). R291 gitgraph's / R292 mindmap's / R293 xychart's tests ALL encoded ``len(_UNSUPPORTED_DIAGRAM_TYPES) == 9``; R294's removal (9 -> 8) breaks all three -- a bucket-guard sync updates each to ``== 8`` with a docstring noting R294's subsequent shrinkage. This is the explicit, documented exception to the "do not break iteration independence" rule (established R282, continued R283-R293), and at 3 synced tests it is the widest bucket-guard churn yet. The feat commit spans 7 files (the family's new widest, surpassing R293's 6): the requirement renderer + render dispatch + requirement tests + render tests (parametrize requirementDiagram removed + docstrings) + gitgraph test sync + mindmap test sync + xychart test sync. The barrel ``to_svg.__all__`` stays 18 (R277 baseline) -- requirementDiagram is reached only via the dispatch arm (continues R279-R293). ### Fusion conclusion

erDiagram is the second dagre consumer and the first entity-relationship layout in the family. It builds a ``minimax_code.data_structures.Graph`` with ``GraphOption(directed=True, multigraph=True, compound=False)`` (the same option R294 requirementDiagram chose), hands it to ``dagre_layout``, and consumes the returned node boxes + edge waypoints to emit SVG ``<g>`` entity tables and crow's-foot ``<path>`` connectors. Three load-bearing clone details shape the port. First, **``compound=False`` is deliberate (shared with R294)**: ER diagrams carry no subgraphs, so the graph is built non-compound; this sidesteps the pre-existing ``network_simplex._exchange_edges`` defect (``None -= 1`` on intra-subgraph chained edges, the ``long_identifier`` xfail(strict=True)) by keeping dagre on the plain simplex branch -- the same workaround R294 established, now reused rather than rediscovered. Second, **the SVG root places ``id="my-svg"`` at the TAIL** (grok ``er_diagram.rs``): the root opens ``<svg aria-roledescription="er" role="graphics-document document" [viewBox] [style] class="erDiagram" xmlns:xlink="..." xmlns="..." width="100%" id="my-svg">`` -- ``id="my-svg"`` lands AFTER ``width="100%"``, NOT first like gitgraph's ``<svg id="my-svg" ...>`` head form. The initial dispatch-smoke test anchored on ``'<svg id="my-svg"'`` and failed; grep-verification of grok confirmed the tail position, so the test was relaxed to a position-independent substring ``'id="my-svg"' in svg`` (mirroring R293 xychart's tail-position lesson). Both ``id="my-svg"`` and ``class="erDiagram"`` ARE present, just emitted in grok's er-specific order. Third, **the ``<style>`` block ships the ``.edgeLabel`` CSS selector UNCONDITIONALLY**: grok emits ``#my-svg .edgeLabel .label {fill:#9370DB;font-size:14px;}`` regardless of whether any relationship carries a role. The initial ``test_edge_label_skipped_when_no_role`` asserted a bare ``"edgeLabel"`` substring is absent and failed (the style block always ships it); the fix was to scope the assertion to the per-edge ELEMENT form ``'class="edgeLabel"' not in svg`` -- the quoted attribute isolates the ``<g class="edgeLabel">`` group (emitted only when a role exists) from the CSS selector (always present). Both fixes continue R292's / R293's "implementation-is-source-of-truth" discipline: when implementation (mirroring grok) and test disagree, grep the grok source and correct the test. The functional contract cloned: the ``erDiagram`` header + entity blocks (``ENTITY { type name ... }``) + the ``A <spec> B : role`` relationship line, the typed AST (``EntityNode`` + ``Relationship`` + ``EntityAttribute``), the BTreeMap name-ascending entity order (grok's ``BTreeMap<String, EntityNode>`` traversal), the dagre-backed ``compute_er_box_layout`` (builds ``Graph(compound=False)`` -> ``dagre_layout`` -> reads node boxes + edge waypoints), the four crow's-foot cardinalities (``||`` OnlyOne / ``|o``|``o|`` ZeroOrOne / ``|{``|``}|`` OneOrMore / ``o{``|``}o`` ZeroOrMore) x Start/End markers (8 total, all emitted unconditionally), the Identifying (``--``) / NonIdentifying (``..``) distinction (the latter carries ``stroke-dasharray="8,8"``), the zebra-striped attribute rows (Odd white / Even ``lighten(node_fill, 0.25)``), the type/name two-column layout with a ``.divider``, and the 5-channel theme binding.

This validates the dagre investment as a multi-customer engine rather than a one-off: the rank/order/position pipeline (R250-R268) now serves two distinct diagram families (requirement trees + entity-relationship graphs), and the ``compound=False`` workaround R294 established is reused without modification.
2. **``compound=False`` sidesteps the pre-existing network_simplex defect (reused from R294, L528/L542)** -- ER diagrams carry no subgraphs, so the graph is built non-compound. This is load-bearing: compound graphs route dagre through the ``network_simplex`` path that has the ``_exchange_edges`` ``None -= 1`` defect on intra-subgraph chained edges (the ``long_identifier`` xfail). By staying non-compound, erDiagram avoids triggering the defect while still exercising the full rank/order/position stack. R294 discovered this workaround; R295 reuses it as established doctrine -- the second consumer pays no rediscovery cost.
3. **SVG root ``id="my-svg"`` at the TAIL (grok er_diagram.rs, the load-bearing byte-order detail)** -- grok emits the er root as ``<svg aria-roledescription="er" role="graphics-document document" viewBox="..." style="..." class="erDiagram" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="100%" id="my-svg">``. Note ``id="my-svg"`` comes AFTER ``width="100%"`` -- a THIRD distinct root-attribute order in the family: gitgraph (R291) emits ``id`` at the HEAD (``<svg id="my-svg" ...>``), xychart (R293) emits ``id`` at the TAIL, and erDiagram (R295) also emits ``id`` at the TAIL but with a different attribute sequence (``class`` before ``xmlns``). The initial dispatch-smoke test asserted ``'<svg id="my-svg"' in svg`` (anchored head form) and failed; grep-verification confirmed the tail position, so the test was relaxed to ``'id="my-svg"' in svg`` (non-anchored substring). The ``class="erDiagram"`` token is likewise asserted position-independently. This byte-order fidelity is the R295 analog of R293's tail-position lesson: each renderer's actual emission order is grok's contract, so the test adapts.
4. **unconditional ``.edgeLabel`` CSS selector + per-edge element assertion (the test-calibration detail)** -- grok's ``<style>`` block always ships ``#my-svg .edgeLabel .label {fill:#9370DB;font-size:14px;}`` regardless of whether any relationship carries a role. The ``edgeLabels`` (plural) group wrapper is also always present. So the ONLY signal that a specific edge carries a role is the per-edge ``<g transform="..." class="edgeLabel">`` element (quoted attribute). The initial ``test_edge_label_skipped_when_no_role`` asserted a bare ``"edgeLabel"`` substring is absent and failed (the style selector ships it anyway); the fix was to assert ``'class="edgeLabel"' not in svg`` -- the quoted attribute form isolates the element from the CSS selector. This mirrors the "implementation-is-source-of-truth" discipline: the CSS selector is grok's unconditional emission, the element is the conditional emission, and the test distinguishes them by attribute form rather than substring.
5. **5-channel theme-aware palette (the family's full-theme tier, alongside R289 block + R294 requirement)** -- erDiagram binds 5 theme channels directly (NOT normalized): LIGHT ``background=#ffffff`` / ``node_fill=#ECECFF`` / ``node_stroke=#9370DB`` / ``edge_color=#333333`` / ``text_color=#333333``; DARK ``background=#1e1e1e`` / ``node_fill=#2d2d2d`` / ``node_stroke=#888888`` / ``edge_color=#888888`` / ``text_color=#ffffff``. The zebra stripes derive: LIGHT Odd row is white (``#ffffff``) and Even row is ``lighten(node_fill, 0.25) = #F0F0FF``; DARK derives both stripes from the background (``lighten(#1e1e1e, 0.08) = #303030`` / ``lighten(#1e1e1e, 0.16) = #424242``). The four ``zeroOrOne``/``zeroOrMore`` markers (x4 total) each carry a ``circle fill="white"`` crossbar; the ``onlyOne`` markers carry grok's ``refX="0" refY="9" markerWidth="18" markerHeight="18"`` geometry. The relationship's ``spec`` (e.g. ``||--o{``) splits into ``card_a`` (left) + ``Identification`` (``--`` Identifying / ``..`` NonIdentifying) + ``card_b`` (right): ``marker-start`` binds ``card_a.Start``, ``marker-end`` binds ``card_b.End``, and NonIdentifying edges carry ``stroke-dasharray="8,8"`` while Identifying edges do not. The ``role`` renders as a centred ``<g class="edgeLabel">`` text with ``style="font-size:14px"`` when non-empty, omitted entirely (no element) when absent.

## R296 — migrate grok class_diagram.rs -> render_class_diagram_to_svg (direction (1) brick 27: 18th per-diagram leaf, 17th self-contained SVG emitter, THIRD dagre-consuming renderer)

### Round goal

Port grok ``class_diagram.rs`` (1144 lines) to Python ``render_class_diagram_to_svg`` as a functional clone (not a line-by-line transcription), wiring it into the ``render.py`` dispatch so a ``classDiagram`` mermaid source renders to a self-contained SVG string. This is the 27th brick of direction (1) (activate dagre: mermaid end-to-end rendering), the 18th per-diagram leaf, and the 17th self-contained SVG emitter. **It is also the family's THIRD renderer to consume the dagre layout engine** -- the lineage is now a proven pattern. R279 info / R281 radar / R282 pie / R283 packet / R284 sankey / R285 gantt / R286 kanban / R287 timeline / R288 quadrant / R289 block / R290 journey / R291 gitgraph / R292 mindmap / R293 xychart all emit bespoke geometry; R294 ``requirementDiagram`` was the first dagre customer, R295 ``erDiagram`` the second, and ``classDiagram`` is the third -- reusing the same ``compound=False`` dagre strategy for the third time, so the workaround is now established doctrine rather than a fresh discovery.

### Fusion conclusion

classDiagram is the third dagre consumer and the family's first UML class-hierarchy layout. It builds a ``minimax_code.data_structures.Graph`` with ``GraphOption(directed=True, multigraph=True, compound=False)`` (the same option R294 requirementDiagram and R295 erDiagram chose), hands it to ``dagre_layout``, and consumes the returned node boxes + edge waypoints to emit SVG ``<g>`` class nodes (three-section title / attribute / method tables) and UML ``<path>`` connectors carrying extension/dependency/composition/aggregation/lollipop markers. Five load-bearing clone details shape the port. First, **``compound=False`` is deliberate (shared with R294/R295)**: class diagrams carry no subgraphs, so the graph is built non-compound; this sidesteps the pre-existing ``network_simplex._exchange_edges`` defect (``None -= 1`` on intra-subgraph chained edges, the ``long_identifier`` xfail(strict=True)) by keeping dagre on the plain simplex branch -- the workaround R294 established and R295 reused is now applied for the third time with zero rediscovery cost. Second, **the SVG root carries NO ``id="my-svg"``** (grok ``class_diagram.rs``): the root opens ``<svg xmlns="..." class="classDiagram" viewBox="0 0 {w:.0f} {h:.0f}" role="graphics-document document" aria-roledescription="class">`` -- a FOURTH distinct root-attribute variant in the family: gitgraph (R291) emits ``id`` at the HEAD, xychart (R293) at the TAIL, erDiagram (R295) at the TAIL with a different sequence, and classDiagram (R296) OMITS ``id="my-svg"`` ENTIRELY. The dispatch-smoke test asserts this absence directly (``assert 'id="my-svg"' not in svg``); ``class="classDiagram"`` and ``aria-roledescription="class"`` (NOT ``"classDiagram"`` -- grok's class-specific roledescription token) are asserted position-independently. Third, **the grok class parser has three core contracts** that the port mirrors verbatim: (a) ``rest.strip_suffix('{')`` (grok L218) matches ONLY a line that ENDS with ``{`` -- i.e. a multi-line block opener ``class Name {``; a single-line ``class Name {}`` (ends with ``}``) does NOT match and falls to the setdefault branch, which would pollute the key with the whole ``"Name {}"`` string; (b) ``line.split_once(':')`` (grok L279/L365-L382) drives the single-line member append -- the form is ``Dog : +bark() String`` (colon separator), NOT ``Dog.bark()`` (dot form raises ``ParseError`` in grok too); (c) ``classify_members`` (grok L416-L424) stores the member string VERBATIM by ``if m.contains('(') { methods } else { attrs }`` -- no field/type/visibility parsing, so ``+bark() String`` is stored whole as one method entry. Fourth, **nine UML markers ship in ``<defs>``** (not eight): extension (hollow triangle, ``<|--`` inheritance, ``fill="transparent"``) + dependency (filled arrowhead, ``-->``, ``fill="{edge_color}"``) + composition (filled diamond, ``fill="{edge_color}"``) + aggregation (hollow diamond, ``fill="transparent"``) each as Start + End = 8, PLUS lollipop (circle, interface) Start-only = 9 total; every marker carries ``refY="7"``, ``class="marker <type>"``, ``stroke="{edge_color}" stroke-width="1"``, with Start markers using ``markerWidth="190" markerHeight="240"`` (refX=18 for extension/composition/aggregation, refX=6 for dependency, refX=13 for lollipop) and End markers using ``markerWidth="20" markerHeight="28"`` refX=1. Edge marker references are PREFIXLESS (``url(#extensionStart)``) -- unlike erDiagram's ``url(#my-svg_er-onlyOneStart)``; the absence of ``id="my-svg"`` on the root is consistent with this. Fifth, **the edge path uses the one-decimal ``M{x:.1},{y:.1}`` form** (``_fmt1``) while the viewBox and node rects use the integer-dropping ``_fmt`` (Rust f64 Display): the first ``d="M`` substring in the emitted SVG belongs to a marker triangle (integer coords like ``M 1,7 L18,13 V 1 Z``), so the edge-path-form test locates the relation path's own ``d`` via ``svg.rindex('d="', 0, svg.index('class="relation"'))`` (reverse search up to the ``class="relation"`` anchor) rather than the naive first-match. The functional contract cloned: the ``classDiagram`` header + ``class Name { members }`` blocks (members split by ``(`` into attrs vs methods, ``<<x>>`` stereotype lines, ``%%``/blank skipping) + the ``A <||-- B : label`` relationship lines (with optional quoted cardinalities ``"1" --> "many"`` spliced into the label) + the ``direction LR`` directive, the typed AST (``ClassInfo`` + ``ClassRelationship`` + ``RelationshipKind`` + ``Direction``), the BTreeMap name-ascending class order (grok's ``BTreeMap<String, ClassInfo>`` traversal, rebuilt via a sorted-dict reconstruction at parse end), the dagre-backed ``compute_class_box_layout`` (builds ``Graph(compound=False)`` -> ``dagre_layout`` -> reads node boxes + edge waypoints), the 9-marker UML system, the dashed distinction (realization ``<|..`` / dependency ``..>`` carry ``stroke-dasharray="3"``), the three-section class node (title / attribute-divider / method-divider with ``<<x>>`` -> ``«x»`` guillemet stereotype), and the 5-channel theme binding.

### Round goal

Port grok ``c4_diagram.rs`` (1201 lines) to Python ``render_c4_diagram_to_svg`` as a functional clone (not a line-by-line transcription), wiring it into the ``render.py`` dispatch so that all FIVE C4 diagram-type tokens (``C4Context`` / ``C4Container`` / ``C4Component`` / ``C4Dynamic`` / ``C4Deployment``) render through ONE shared renderer to a self-contained SVG string. This is the 28th brick of direction (1), the 19th per-diagram leaf, the 18th self-contained SVG emitter, and the largest single migration in the family (5 unsupported tokens removed at once). **It is also the brick that BREAKS the dagre-consumer streak**: R294 requirementDiagram / R295 erDiagram / R296 classDiagram were three consecutive dagre customers, and R296's roadmap predicted "the next renderer likely to consume dagre (C4 context/container/component nesting layout)" -- R297 FALSIFIES that prediction. C4 does NOT touch the dagre engine at all; it self-computes shape coordinates through a bespoke flowing-grid layout (a port of Mermaid's ``Bounds`` class). The dagre-consumer family therefore stays at three (R294/R295/R296), and C4 rejoins the bespoke-geometry family that R279-R293 built.

### Fusion conclusion

C4 is the family's first 5-variant single-renderer migration and its first Structurizr C4-model layout. Where every prior per-diagram leaf mapped one diagram token to one renderer, C4 maps FIVE tokens (``C4Context`` / ``C4Container`` / ``C4Component`` / ``C4Dynamic`` / ``C4Deployment``) to ONE entry ``render_c4_diagram_to_svg``, and the only per-variant divergence is a single render-time branch: ``C4Dynamic`` prefixes each relationship label with its 1-based index (``f"{i + 1}: {rel.label}"``, grok L1154-L1158, Python L1085), the other four emit the label verbatim. Six load-bearing clone details shape the port. First, **C4 does NOT consume dagre (the streak-breaker, falsifies R296's roadmap prediction)**: the module's imports are ``math`` / ``OrderedDict`` / ``dataclasses`` / ``ParseError`` / ``MermaidTheme`` ONLY -- no ``Graph``, no ``dagre_layout``, no ``GraphOption``. C4 uses a bespoke flowing-grid geometry: shapes are placed 4-per-row wrapping at ``width_limit=800`` via the ``_Bounds`` tracker, a 9-field port of Mermaid's ``Bounds`` class (grok L127-L210, Python L254). The docstring (L9-L16) declares this contract explicitly and contrasts it with the dagre consumers (R294/R295/R296). This is the single most important R297 finding: the dagre engine's customer count is NOT monotonically growing -- some diagram families self-lay, and C4 is the largest such family. Second, **9 C4 shape types x 2 = 18 colour mappings** (grok L23-L73): each shape type (``system`` / ``container`` / ``component`` / ``containerDb`` / ``containerQueue`` / ``componentDb`` / ``componentQueue`` / ``person`` / ``external_*`` twins) has a base fill and a ``_BORDER_COLOR_FOR`` stroke, carried in two lookup tables with a single ``default`` fallback. Third, **3 shape geometries**: rectangle (default), database cylinder (``*_db`` types), queue (``*_queue`` types); ``person`` / ``external_person`` additionally carry a 48x48 PNG icon (``PERSON_IMG`` / ``EXTERNAL_PERSON_IMG`` raw ``data:image/png`` URIs, kept verbatim byte-for-byte including the legacy non-ASCII byte sequence on the EXTERNAL variant). Fourth, **boundaries are dashed ``#444444`` rectangles** wrapping child shapes, with a bold label + optional ``[type]`` subtitle (grok L968-L1003). Fifth, **relationships are first-straight-then-Bézier**: the first rel renders a straight ``<line>``, subsequent rels render quadratic Bézier ``<path>`` curves; all carry the ``arrowhead`` marker and an optional ``[techn]`` italic subtitle (grok L1134-L1201). Sixth, **static ``<defs>`` ship unconditionally**: 3 icon ``<symbol>`` (computer/database/clock) + 4 arrow ``<marker>`` (arrowhead/arrowend/crosshead/filled-head) are emitted on every render (grok L950-L966), regardless of whether the diagram references them. The theme contract is NARROWER than the dagre consumers: only 3 of the 5 channels flow in -- ``background`` (svg ``background-color``, normalised ``#ffffff`` -> ``white``), ``text_color`` (style ``fill``, normalised ``#333333`` -> ``#333``), ``edge_color`` (the ``.marker`` class fill/stroke); the shape/boundary palette is fixed C4 (the 18 mapping tables are constant, not theme-derived). The Pythonic conversions are mechanical and behaviour-preserving: ``estimate_text_width`` uses ``len(text.encode('utf-8'))`` to mirror Rust's ``str::len()`` (byte length); ``_Bounds`` is a plain ``@dataclass`` with explicit ``set_data`` / ``insert`` / ``bump_last_margin`` methods porting grok's insert algorithm verbatim including the ``next_cnt > C4_SHAPE_IN_ROW`` row-wrap reset; the parser is split into pure functions (``_parse_c4_diagram`` / ``_parse_c4_statement`` / ``_find_matching_paren`` / ``_split_c4_args``) matching grok's line-oriented state machine. The dispatch wiring in ``render.py`` (L499-L505) matches all five C4 tokens in one ``if diagram_type in (...)`` arm BEFORE the ``_UNSUPPORTED_DIAGRAM_TYPES`` check (L507), so the five tokens never reach the unsupported surface; ``_UNSUPPORTED_DIAGRAM_TYPES`` shrinks 6 -> 1 (only ``sequenceDiagram`` remains).

### Round goal

Port grok ``sequence_diagram.rs`` (1326 lines) to Python ``render_sequence_diagram_to_svg`` as a functional clone (not a line-by-line transcription), wiring it into the ``render.py`` dispatch so that the ``sequenceDiagram`` token renders through a dedicated renderer to a self-contained SVG string. This is the 29th brick of direction (1), the 20th per-diagram leaf, the 19th self-contained SVG emitter, and **the LAST per-diagram renderer in the family** -- after R298, every grok ``mermaid-to-svg`` per-diagram renderer is migrated, and ``_UNSUPPORTED_DIAGRAM_TYPES`` EMPTIES from 1 -> 0 (the unsupported-type raise becomes a dead branch that can never fire). Like R297 C4, sequenceDiagram does NOT consume the dagre engine: it uses a bespoke sequence-timing geometry (fixed participant columns + a 37px event-row grid + activation-bar stacking + fragment nesting-depth inset), so the dagre-consumer family stays at three (R294/R295/R296) and sequenceDiagram rejoins the bespoke-geometry family that R279-R293 + R297 built. R298 therefore CLOSES the per-diagram migration arc of direction (1); what remains is the dagre edge-swap defect tail (flip the ``long_identifier`` xfail) and then direction (1) itself closes.

### Fusion conclusion

sequenceDiagram is the family's last leaf and its only UML interaction-diagram layout. Where the prior 18 emitters covered flowchart/state/info/radar/pie/packet/sankey/gantt/kanban/timeline/quadrant/block/journey/gitGraph/mindmap/xychart/requirement/er/class/C4, the sequence diagram poses a fundamentally different layout problem: it is NOT a node-edge graph at all, it is a TIME-DOMAIN grid where participants are COLUMNS (lifelines) and messages are HORIZONTAL ROWS between columns. Six load-bearing clone details shape the port. First, **sequenceDiagram does NOT consume dagre (the second consecutive dagre-free emitter, confirms R297's streak-break was not a one-off)**: the module's imports (L98-L105) are ``from __future__ import annotations`` / ``from dataclasses import dataclass, field`` / ``from enum import Enum`` / ``ParseError`` / ``display_width_units`` / ``MermaidTheme`` ONLY -- no ``Graph``, no ``dagre_layout``, no ``GraphOption``. The geometry is self-contained arithmetic: participants become fixed-width columns at computed x-offsets (``_compute_sequence_pair_spacings``, L1285), events stack down a 37px-row grid, activation bars widen the lifeline into a stacked rectangle, and fragments (alt/loop/opt/par/critical/break/rect) inset by their nesting depth. Second, **10 arrow kinds in a fixity-ordered dispatch table** (``_ARROWS``, L842): a 4-tuple of ``(token, dashed, head, bidirectional)`` tried longest-first so ``<<-->>`` matches before ``-->>`` before ``->>`` before ``->>`` etc. The 4 ``_ArrowHead`` variants (L143: ``FILLED`` / ``CROSS`` / ``OPEN`` / ``NONE``) select the marker; ``dashed`` toggles ``stroke-dasharray="5,4"``; ``bidirectional`` adds a ``marker-start`` reverse arrowhead. Third, **7 fragment kinds** (``_FragmentKind``, L152: ``ALT`` / ``LOOP`` / ``OPT`` / ``PAR`` / ``CRITICAL`` / ``BREAK`` / ``RECT``) each open a nesting level that an ``end`` closes (``_FragmentEnd`` identity sentinel L266); ``else`` / ``and`` / ``option`` push sibling branches inside an open fragment (``_FragmentElse``). Fourth, **autonumber** (``_AutoNumber``, L346): a stateful counter that prepends ``N. `` to each message label when active, with ``autonumber N S`` setting the start + step and ``autonumber off`` deactivating. Fifth, **notes + activation bars**: ``Note left/of A: text`` / ``Note over A: text`` / ``Note A->B: text`` place a sticky note (``_Note``, L229) beside or over a lifeline; ``A->>+B`` activates B's lifeline (``_Activate``, L237) and ``B-->>-A`` deactivates B (the ``+``/``-`` suffixes on the arrow endpoints). Sixth, **the theme contract is 4-of-5 channels**: ``background`` (canvas rect), ``node_fill`` + ``node_stroke`` (participant head/foot boxes, activation bars, fragment tabs), ``edge_color`` (lifeline stroke, message stroke, arrowhead fill, note border), ``text_color`` (participant labels, message text). The NOTE interior is hardcoded (``#fff2b0`` fill / ``#333333`` text), and the fragment border/tab are hardcoded (``_SEQ_FRAG_STROKE = "#d7c8f8"`` L130, ``_SEQ_FRAG_TEXT = "#4c3f6f"`` L132) -- cloning grok's fixed note + fragment palette verbatim. The Pythonic conversions are mechanical: ``_SequenceEvent`` is a union of 7 event types (L275, ``X | Y`` form after the UP007 ruff fix); ``display_width_units`` (from R273 text_wrap) replaces Rust's ``str::len()`` for label-width heuristics so CJK / wide-glyph labels measure correctly; the parser is split into pure functions (``_strip_keyword_ci`` L610 / ``_parse_message_line`` L856 / ``_parse_fragment_line`` L914) matching grok's line-oriented state machine. The dispatch wiring in ``render.py`` (L524) matches the ``sequenceDiagram`` token in its own arm BEFORE the ``_UNSUPPORTED_DIAGRAM_TYPES`` check (L527, now an empty set), so the token never reaches the unsupported surface; ``_UNSUPPORTED_DIAGRAM_TYPES`` EMPTIES 1 -> 0.

There is NO ``from minimax_code.data_structures.graph import Graph`` and NO ``from minimax_code.mermaid.dagre import dagre_layout``. ## R299 — restore grok no-op contract in graphlib ``_decrement_or_remove_entry`` (direction (1) TAIL: fix dagre ``network_simplex._exchange_edges`` ``None -= 1`` TypeError, flip ``long_identifier`` ``xfail(strict=True)`` -> xpass, CLOSES direction (1))

Anchor:R299-1 <pending>

### Round goal

Close the last direction-(1) tail item: the dagre ``network_simplex._exchange_edges`` ``None -= 1`` TypeError that held ``test_long_identifier_node_labels_survive_intact_in_svg`` under ``xfail(strict=True)`` since R278c. The defect lives in ``graphlib.py`` ``_decrement_or_remove_entry``: the R269-R271 multigraph port dropped grok's ``if let Some(value) = map.get_mut(k)`` missing-key guard, so a ``remove_edge`` that hits an edge object whose endpoint was never seeded into the peer's counter map dereferences ``None`` and crashes. R299 restores grok's no-op contract (a MISSING key is a no-op, matching graph.rs L899-L906 verbatim in behaviour), flips the ``long_identifier`` xfail to a real pass, and CLOSES direction (1). This is a behaviour-equivalence restoration, NOT new surface: zero new modules, zero new public symbols, zero new tests (the existing xfail is un-decorated, not replaced). The clone-by-function methodology held -- the fix was reached by grepping grok's source-of-truth ``decrement_or_remove_entry`` and restoring its guard, not by inventing Pythonic behaviour.

### Fusion conclusion

The crash is a faithful-clone defect, not a design gap. grok's ``graphlib_rust`` models a multigraph as a node map whose per-edge endpoints carry parallel-edge counter maps (``_preds[w]`` counts how many edges ``v -> w`` exist; ``_sucs[v]`` mirrors for successors). The invariant grok relies on is NOT "an edge object and its counter-map keys always agree" -- under the anonymous-edge (``name = None``) semantics that dagre's ``network_simplex`` uses for its internal spanning-tree bookkeeping, an edge object can exist in the edge set while one of its endpoints was never seeded into the peer's counter map. grok tolerates this asymmetry by guarding EVERY counter-map mutation with ``if let Some``: a missing key is a silent no-op. The R269-R271 Python port transcribed the happy path (``value -= 1``; drop at zero) but lost the guard, so the first time ``network_simplex`` swapped a tree edge whose back-edge endpoint was a synthesised tree node (``_bt*``), ``_decrement_or_remove_entry`` called ``counter_map.get(key)``, got ``None``, and executed ``None -= 1``. Four load-bearing facts shape the fix. First, **the trigger is ``network_simplex._exchange_edges`` (network_simplex.py L362-L375)**: when the rank solver swaps tree edge ``e`` for non-tree edge ``f``, it calls ``t.remove_edge(v, w, None)`` on the spanning-tree graph ``t``. The edge object ``(v, w, None)`` exists in ``t``'s edge set (it was inserted as an anonymous tree edge), but ``_preds[w]`` -- the predecessor counter map for ``w`` -- was seeded with the ORIGINAL spanning-tree node id (e.g. ``'nav'``), NOT the post-exchange back-edge tree node id (``'_bt2'``). So ``t.remove_edge('nav', '_bt2', None)`` finds the edge object, then tries to decrement ``_preds['_bt2']`` which is absent. Second, **the multigraph counter map is the structural reason the asymmetry is LEGAL, not a bug**: an edge object in a multigraph is identified by ``(v, w, name)``; the counter map ``_preds[w]`` is an auxiliary index that maps a predecessor ``v`` to how many parallel ``v -> w`` edges exist. Under anonymous edges (``name = None``) -- which dagre uses for its internal spanning forest -- an edge can be inserted via a path that updates the edge set but not both counter maps (e.g. tree construction seeds ``_sucs`` but the back-edge re-entry does not re-seed ``_preds`` for a synthesised node). grok's design accepts this: the counter map is a best-effort parallel index, and ``decrement_or_remove_entry`` treats a missing key as "nothing to decrement" (no-op). Third, **grok's guard is exactly two lines** (graph.rs L899-L906): ``if let Some(value) = map.get_mut(k) { *value -= 1; if *value <= 0 { map.remove(k); } }`` -- the entire body is conditionally skipped when the key is absent. The Python port had ``value = counter_map.get(key)`` followed unconditionally by ``value -= 1``, dropping the conditional. Fourth, **the fix is a no-op restoration, NOT a "treat None as 0" hack**: restoring the guard means a missing key does NOTHING (no insertion, no decrement), exactly matching grok. The alternative -- ``counter_map.get(key, 0) - 1`` then insert -- would WRONGLY insert a negative-count entry and diverge from grok's "missing means absent, not zero" contract. The Pythonic conversion is therefore: ``value = counter_map.get(key); if value is None: return; value -= 1; if value <= 0: counter_map.remove(key) else: counter_map.insert(key, value)``. Position-preserving above zero (matching grok's in-place ``*value -= 1`` via ``OrderedHashMap.insert`` which updates in place for an existing key), drop entirely at zero. The ``long_identifier`` xfail -- which guarded a real-user flowchart with a compound ``subgraph`` + a 4-edge chain whose layout exercised the ``_exchange_edges`` path -- now passes because the swap no longer crashes; the compound subgraph lays out and each long identifier reaches the SVG as one complete ``<tspan>``.

### Evidence

1. **grok source-of-truth guard (graph.rs L899-L906)** -- ``fn decrement_or_remove_entry<K: Hash + Eq + Clone>(map: &mut OrderedHashMap<K, usize>, k: &K) { if let Some(value) = map.get_mut(k) { *value -= 1; if *value <= 0 { map.remove(k); } } }``. The ENTIRE body is inside the ``if let Some`` -- a missing ``k`` skips the block, a no-op. This is the contract R299 restores.
2. **crash root-cause reproduced under the grok invariant** -- the synthesised minimal repro: ``counter_map = OrderedHashMap({'nav': 1})`` (the predecessor index for ``w``, seeded with the original tree node), ``key = '_bt2'`` (the post-exchange back-edge tree node). ``_decrement_or_remove_entry(counter_map, '_bt2')`` called ``counter_map.get('_bt2')`` -> ``None`` -> ``None -= 1`` -> ``TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for -=: 'NoneType' and 'int'``. The edge object ``('nav', '_bt2', None)`` EXISTS in the graph's edge set; only the counter-map key is absent -- the legal multigraph asymmetry. Pre-fix: TypeError. Post-fix: no-op, ``counter_map`` unchanged.
3. **trigger path: ``network_simplex._exchange_edges`` (network_simplex.py L362-L375)** -- L371 ``t.remove_edge(v, w, None)`` is the crash call. The main loop (L143) invokes ``_exchange_edges(t, simplified, e, f)`` to swap tree edge ``e`` for non-tree edge ``f`` during rank optimisation. ``Graph.remove_edge`` (graphlib.py L885) resolves the edge object (found, since the tree edge was inserted), then calls ``_decrement_or_remove_entry(preds, v_canon)`` where ``preds = self._preds[w_canon]`` -- and ``v_canon`` (the back-edge tree node ``_bt*``) is absent. R298's sequenceDiagram never reached this path because it does not consume dagre (R298 Evidence #1); R294/R295/R296 (the three dagre-consumers) reach it but their test fixtures do not exercise a back-edge swap into a synthesised tree node, so the defect stayed latent until the ``long_identifier`` compound-subgraph flowchart (which has enough rank-crossing edges to force ``_exchange_edges`` over a ``_bt*`` node).
4. **fix restores grok's no-op contract (graphlib.py L1020-L1042)** -- ``_decrement_or_remove_entry`` now reads: ``value = counter_map.get(key); if value is None: return  # grok: missing key -> no-op (the `if let Some` guard).; value -= 1; if value <= 0: counter_map.remove(key); else: counter_map.insert(key, value)``. The docstring records the grok reference (L899-L906), the legal-asymmetry invariant (multigraph anonymous-edge ``name = None`` semantics where ``remove_edge`` can hit an edge object whose endpoint was never seeded into the peer's counter map), the specific trigger (dagre ``network_simplex`` back-edge tree nodes ``_bt*``), and that the R269-R271 port lost this guard and crashed on ``None -= 1``. Two lines of executable code (the ``if value is None: return`` guard) plus the docstring rewrite.
5. **xfail -> xpass flip (test_mermaid_pure.py L269-L304)** -- ``test_long_identifier_node_labels_survive_intact_in_svg`` was ``@pytest.mark.xfail(strict=True, reason=...)`` from R278c; the decorator (15 lines, original L269-L283) is removed entirely, and the diagnostic history is folded into the test docstring (``History:`` paragraph naming the defect path, the grok guard, the R269-R271 drop, and R299's restoration). The test body (the ``subgraph main [resi_local.py / resi.py]`` + ``nav --> mark --> global --> sidebar --> page`` chain, asserting ``>mark_filter_restore_context</tspan>`` and ``>render_page_sidebar_filters</tspan>`` survive intact) is unchanged. With the guard restored the compound subgraph lays out and both identifiers reach the SVG as single complete ``<tspan>``s -- a real pass, no longer an expected failure.
6. **the fix is upstream of every dagre-consumer, not a per-consumer patch** -- ``_decrement_or_remove_entry`` is used by ``Graph.remove_edge`` (the single call site), which is used by ``network_simplex._exchange_edges`` (the rank solver), which is consumed by R294 requirement / R295 er / R296 class (the three dagre-consumers) AND by the ``long_identifier`` compound-subgraph path. Fixing the guard in ``graphlib.py`` fixes the contract for ALL present and future dagre layouts -- one two-line restoration, family-wide effect. No dagre-consumer renderer or test was touched; the fix is purely in the shared data-structure layer.

### Round goal

Open direction (2) by landing its first brick: port grok's ``xai-codebase-graph`` crate's ``types/`` subpackage to Python under ``minimax_code.xai_codebase_graph.types``. R299's roadmap named direction (2) (the tree-sitter code index) the active P0 front once direction (1) closed; R300 narrows to the type foundation only -- the 4 grok source files ``types/range.rs`` (``Position`` + ``Range``) + ``types/location.rs`` (``Location``) + ``types/file_event.rs`` (``FileEvent``) + the structural types defined inline in ``types/mod.rs`` (``IndexStats`` / ``SymbolOccurrence`` / ``SymbolAlias`` / ``FileMeta``). This slice is chosen first because it is cohesive (a single ``types/`` directory), zero-external-dependency (Python stdlib + ``dataclasses`` only -- no tree-sitter, no serde, no pydantic), and the type layer that EVERY downstream slice (``scope_graph/``, ``interner/``, ``languages/``, ``manager/``, ``navigation``) consumes: ``Range`` and ``Location`` are the coordinate vocabulary of every symbol/edge query, ``FileEvent`` drives the live-index update loop, ``FileMeta`` backs staleness detection. The clone-by-function methodology held: grok's functional contract is preserved verbatim in behaviour (``Position`` 0-indexed-internal / 1-indexed-public accessors; ``Range`` LSP-compatible inclusive bounds; ``FileEvent`` 4-variant path/reparse/affects-existing contract; ``FileMeta`` ``os.stat`` mtime secs+nanos split with pre-epoch ``(0, 0)``), while the implementation is Pythonic (``@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)`` mirroring grok's ``#[derive(Copy, Clone, Hash, PartialEq, Eq)]``; direct attribute access replacing grok's getter methods; a single tagged dataclass + ``FileEventKind`` enum + factory classmethods replacing grok's enum-with-payload). Three YAGNI boundaries are documented in source (NOT implemented): the tree-sitter bridge methods land with ``languages/``; the in-place mutators are replaced by ``dataclasses.replace``; serde (``Serialize`` / ``Deserialize``) lands with the ``manager/`` cache migration where it is consumed. This brick opens direction (2); it does not close it.

### Fusion conclusion

grok's ``xai-codebase-graph`` crate models a codebase as a tree-sitter-backed symbol/edge index: it parses files into definitions and references, tracks file metadata for incremental updates, and serves scope-graph queries for navigation and code review. The type layer is the crate's coordinate vocabulary -- ``Position`` (line + character + byte_offset) and ``Range`` (start + end ``Position``) are LSP-compatible primitives; ``Location`` binds a ``Range`` to a file path; ``FileEvent`` describes the file-system changes that trigger an index update; ``FileMeta`` captures the size + mtime the indexer compares to detect staleness without re-reading contents. The Python port fuses grok's ``Copy + Hash + PartialEq + Eq`` derive story into a single ``@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)`` decision: frozen gives value-equality + hashability + immutability (covering ``PartialEq + Eq + Hash``), slots gives the compact layout grok's ``Copy`` stack-allocation implies, and the absence of ``Copy`` semantics in Python is immaterial because every grok ``Copy`` call site (``let p = self.start_position``) maps to a reference bind in Python with no need to clone. Six load-bearing facts shape the port. First, **grok's getter-method API shape is flattened to direct attribute access**: grok exposes ``rng.start_position()`` (a method returning the private field), but Python exposes ``rng.start_position`` directly (the field IS the public surface); the 1-indexed accessors (``line_1indexed`` / ``column_1indexed`` / ``line_0indexed`` / ``column_0indexed``) STAY as methods because they compute (``+1`` / ``saturating_sub``), and ``column`` is a read-only ``@property`` alias for ``character`` (LSP terminology) rather than a stored field. Second, **``FileEvent``'s 4-variant tagged enum collapses to a single frozen dataclass + a ``FileEventKind`` enum + factory classmethods**: grok models ``Created{path}`` / ``Modified{path}`` / ``Deleted{path}`` / ``Renamed{from, to}`` as enum variants carrying payload; Python has no enum-with-payload, so the port uses ONE dataclass (``kind: FileEventKind`` discriminator + ``path: str`` carrying the primary path + ``from_path: str | None`` carrying the rename source) with four factory constructors (``created`` / ``modified`` / ``deleted`` / ``renamed``) that mirror variant construction and three query methods (``primary_path`` / ``requires_reparse`` / ``affects_existing``) that mirror grok's ``path()`` / ``requires_reparse()`` / ``affects_existing()``. The ``Renamed`` convention is preserved exactly: ``path`` stores the ``to`` target so ``primary_path()`` returns it (matching grok ``path()`` returning ``to`` for renames). Third, **``Arc<str>`` becomes plain ``str``**: grok uses ``Arc<str>`` for ``SymbolOccurrence.name`` / ``SymbolAlias.alias`` / ``SymbolAlias.original`` to share the string cheaply across index merges; Python ``str`` is already interned / reference-shared, so the field is a plain ``str`` with no wrapper. Fourth, **``FileMeta::from_metadata(std::fs::Metadata)`` becomes ``FileMeta.from_stat(os.stat_result)``**: grok splits ``Duration::since(UNIX_EPOCH)`` into ``secs`` + ``subsec_nanos``; the Python port splits ``os.stat_result.st_mtime_ns`` into ``mtime_secs = ns // 1_000_000_000`` + ``mtime_nanos = ns % 1_000_000_000``, and grok's ``unwrap_or((0, 0))`` (the ``Duration`` error for pre-epoch mtimes) maps to an explicit ``if mtime_ns < 0: (0, 0)`` guard (Python's ``st_mtime_ns`` can be negative on systems with pre-epoch file mtimes). Fifth, **the duplicate-type trap is preserved 1:1 (NOT unified)**: grok ships BOTH ``types::Location`` AND ``navigation::Location``, and BOTH ``types::FileEvent`` AND ``index_manager::FileEvent`` under different module paths -- the crate re-publishes a type under each consumer's namespace rather than sharing one definition. The Python port keeps this 1:1: ``minimax_code.xai_codebase_graph.types.Location`` is distinct from the (future) ``navigation.Location``, and ``types.FileEvent`` is distinct from the (future) ``index_manager.FileEvent``; unifying them would diverge from grok's module topology. Sixth, **frozen+slots+property interaction surfaces a non-obvious error type**: assigning to a read-only ``@property`` on a ``frozen=True, slots=True`` dataclass raises ``TypeError: super(type, obj): obj must be an instance or subtype of type`` (the dataclass ``__setattr__`` + the property descriptor interaction), NOT the ``AttributeError`` a plain frozen dataclass raises for a missing slot; the test that asserts ``column`` is read-only therefore accepts BOTH ``AttributeError`` and ``TypeError`` (the point under test is that the assignment is REJECTED, not which exception class). The ``from dataclasses import dataclass, field`` import is load-bearing for ``Range``'s default-``Position`` fields (``field(default_factory=Position)``), because a frozen dataclass cannot hold a mutable default reference and ``Position()`` is the per-instance origin default.

### Evidence

1. **``range.py`` Position (range.rs L13-L130) -- frozen+slots dataclass mirrors grok ``#[derive(Hash, Copy)]``** -- fields ``line`` / ``character`` / ``byte_offset`` (default 0); ``column`` is a ``@property`` alias for ``character`` (grok ``column()`` LSP alias); ``to_byte_offset()`` passthrough; ``line_1indexed()`` / ``column_1indexed()`` (``+1``); ``before_other`` / ``after_other`` (inclusive at equal column, range.rs L89-L96); ``from_byte(cls, byte, line_end_indices)`` classmethod reconstructs (line, column) from a byte offset (range.rs L99-L112), preserving grok's ``unwrap_or(0)`` quirk (the line is the first index whose end-byte EXCEEDS the byte; if none does, the column falls back to 0); ``shift_column(column_move)`` (1-indexed ``saturating_sub(1)``, byte reset, range.rs L115-L121); ``move_to_next_line()`` (range.rs L124-L129). Position is hashable and rejects attribute mutation (``FrozenInstanceError``).
2. **``range.py`` Range (range.rs L151-L365) -- the LSP-compatible coordinate primitive** -- ``start_position`` / ``end_position`` fields (``field(default_factory=Position)``); the full byte/line/column accessor family (0/1-indexed, start/end); ``byte_size()`` (``end - start + 1``), ``len()`` (``end - start``), ``is_empty()``, ``line_size()`` (may be negative); the contains family (``contains`` / ``contains_check_line`` / ``contains_check_line_column`` / ``contains_position`` / ``contains_line``, all inclusive bounds); ``intersects_without_byte()`` (line-based); ``check_equality_without_byte()`` + ``equals_line_range()``; ``from_byte_range(cls, start, end, line_end_indices)`` classmethod building both endpoints. Range is frozen + hashable.
3. **``location.py`` Location (location.rs) -- binds a Range to a file path** -- fields ``file_path: Path`` / ``line: int`` / ``column: int`` / ``range: Range``; ``new()`` classmethod (explicit 1-indexed); ``from_range(cls, file_path, range)`` classmethod (auto-converts from the range's 1-indexed start, location.rs L43-L50); ``path()`` alias; ``extension()`` (strips the leading dot, grok ``PathBuf::extension`` semantics); ``parent_dir()`` (grok's ``Some("")`` for a bare filename normalised to Python ``None``); ``line_0indexed()`` / ``column_0indexed()`` (``saturating_sub``); ``__str__`` = ``file:line:column`` (grok ``Display``). Location is frozen + hashable.

### YAGNI boundaries

- **tree-sitter bridge methods dropped (faithful-clone boundary, land with ``languages/``)** -- grok's ``Position`` carries ``from_tree_sitter_point`` / ``Range`` carries ``from_tree_sitter_node`` bridge methods that convert tree-sitter's ``Point`` / ``Node`` types. These require the ``tree-sitter`` Python binding, which is NOT a dependency of the type layer (the types are stdlib + ``dataclasses`` only). The bridge methods land with the ``languages/`` migration (R302+), which is where tree-sitter is first consumed; R300 documents the deferral in the source docstring rather than stubbing an unusable method.
- **in-place mutators dropped, replaced by ``dataclasses.replace`` (Pythonic-shape boundary)** -- grok's ``Position`` / ``Range`` are BOTH ``Hash`` AND carry ``&mut self`` mutators (``set_byte_offset`` / ``shift_to`` / etc.), exploiting Rust's separate ``&self`` / ``&mut self`` borrow story. Python ``frozen=True`` makes the type immutable (the ``Hash`` half); the mutators are therefore DROPPED, and callers that need a patched copy use ``dataclasses.replace(pos, byte_offset=new)`` -- the standard Pythonic frozen-dataclass idiom. This is the same frozen-vs-mutable tension R274's layout types resolved: keep the type hashable, push mutation to the call site.
- **serde dropped (land with ``manager/`` cache migration)** -- grok derives ``Serialize`` / ``Deserialize`` on ``FileMeta`` (and several types) for on-disk cache persistence. R300's type layer is stdlib-only (no serde / no pydantic); cache (de)serialization lands with the ``manager/`` migration, which is where it is actually consumed. Documented in ``mod.py``'s module docstring.
- **duplicate types preserved 1:1 (NOT unified -- grok-topology boundary)** -- grok ships ``types::Location`` AND ``navigation::Location``, AND ``types::FileEvent`` AND ``index_manager::FileEvent``, as separately-published types under each consumer's module path. ### Round goal

Land direction (2)'s second brick: port grok's ``xai-codebase-graph`` crate's ``scope_graph/`` node / edge TYPE layer to Python under ``minimax_code.xai_codebase_graph.scope_graph``. R300's roadmap named ``scope_graph/edges.py`` + ``scope_graph/nodes.py`` the next brick once the ``types/`` foundation landed; R301 narrows to the two type-bearing source files only -- grok ``scope_graph/edges.rs`` (the ``EdgeKind`` relation label) + ``scope_graph/nodes.rs`` (the six node value types ``Symbol`` / ``SymbolId`` / ``LocalScope`` / ``LocalDef`` / ``LocalImport`` / ``Reference`` + the ``NodeKind`` tagged union). This slice is chosen second because it is the data model EVERY scope-graph query indexes: a scope graph is a per-file collection of nodes (scopes / defs / imports / references) linked by edges, and these types ARE that collection's element vocabulary. The slice is cohesive (a single ``scope_graph/`` directory's two leaf modules), zero-external-dependency (Python stdlib + ``dataclasses`` + ``enum`` only -- no tree-sitter, no ``interner``, no serde, no petgraph), and consumes exactly R300's ``Range`` type (every node carries a ``Range`` for its source span). The ``scope_graph/graph.rs`` RUNTIME (``ScopeGraph`` / ``build_scope_graph`` / ``ScopeGraphResult`` / ``extract_symbols_fast`` / ``QueryVersion`` / ``Snippet``) is explicitly DEFERRED -- it depends on ``interner.rs`` + the ``tree_sitter`` crate + ``languages/``, none of which exist yet; R301 lands only the type layer that runtime will populate. The clone-by-function methodology held: grok's functional contract is preserved verbatim in behaviour (``SymbolId::name`` returns ``None`` on either index out-of-bounds matching grok's ``.get()`` -> ``Option``; ``LocalDef::name(src)`` slices ``[start_byte, end_byte)`` matching grok's byte-slice contract; ``NodeKind::range`` returns the SCOPE range for ``Def`` while ``NodeKind::identifier_range`` returns the identifier's OWN range -- the distinguishing case; the 5 ``EdgeKind`` variant NAMES are preserved verbatim as enum member values for serde compatibility), while the implementation is Pythonic (``@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)`` mirroring grok's ``#[derive(Copy, Clone, Hash, PartialEq, Eq)]``; ``enum.Enum`` for ``EdgeKind``; a single frozen dataclass + ``NodeKindKind`` discriminator + four optional payload slots collapsing grok's enum-with-payload ``NodeKind``). Three YAGNI boundaries are documented in source (NOT implemented): serde lands with ``manager/``; the ``graph.rs`` runtime lands with its own migration; the ``NodeKind::Def`` / ``Import`` / ``Ref`` dedicated constructors are NOT provided because grok only exposes ``scope(range)`` publicly and builds the other variants inline inside ``graph.rs`` (which does not exist yet). This brick CLOSES the scope_graph type layer and OPENS the graph.rs runtime front.

### Fusion conclusion

grok's ``scope_graph`` models a single source file's symbol topology: it stores the file's definitions (``LocalDef``), references (``Reference``), imports (``LocalImport``) and nested scopes (``LocalScope``), each tagged with a ``NodeKind`` so the graph can dispatch on node type, and links them with ``EdgeKind``-labelled edges (nested-scope links, def/import/ref resolution). The Python port fuses grok's ``Copy + Hash + PartialEq + Eq`` derive story into the SAME ``@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)`` decision R300 established (frozen = value-equality + hashability + immutability covering ``PartialEq + Eq + Hash``; slots = compact layout; absence of ``Copy`` immaterial since grok ``Copy`` call sites map to Python reference binds). Eight load-bearing facts shape the port. First, **``EdgeKind`` is a 5-variant ``enum.Enum`` whose member VALUES are the grok variant names verbatim**: grok's ``EdgeKind`` (``ScopeToScope`` / ``DefToScope`` / ``ImportToScope`` / ``RefToDef`` / ``RefToImport``) derives ``Copy + PartialEq + Eq + Hash + Serialize + Deserialize``; the Python port uses ``enum.Enum`` (member identity gives ``Eq`` / ``Hash`` for free; ``Copy`` is meaningless in Python), and keeps each member's VALUE as the grok variant name string (``SCOPE_TO_SCOPE = "ScopeToScope"``) so a future serde layer can use them as externally-tagged keys without renames -- the member NAMES are Pythonic (SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE) while the VALUES preserve grok's wire identity. Second, **``Symbol.kind`` is a plain ``str`` (``Arc<str>`` -> ``str``)**: grok stores the symbol kind as ``Arc<str>`` to share the kind string cheaply across many symbols; Python ``str`` is already interned / reference-shared, so the field is a plain ``str`` (the same ``Arc<str>`` -> ``str`` note R300 applied to ``SymbolOccurrence`` / ``SymbolAlias``). Third, **``SymbolId::name`` preserves grok's ``.get()`` -> ``Option`` -> ``None`` on EITHER index out-of-bounds**: grok's two-level ``(namespace_idx, symbol_idx)`` lookup uses ``namespaces.get(namespace_idx).and_then(|ns| ns.get(symbol_idx))`` which returns ``None`` if the namespace index OR the symbol index is out of bounds; the Python port mirrors this with two chained bounds checks (``0 <= namespace_idx < len(namespaces)`` then ``0 <= symbol_idx < len(ns)``) returning ``None`` on either failure -- NOT raising ``IndexError`` (grok's ``Option`` semantics are total, never panicking). Fourth, **``name(src: bytes) -> bytes`` preserves the byte-slice contract verbatim**: grok's ``LocalDef::name`` / ``LocalImport::name`` / ``Reference::name`` take ``src: &[u8]`` (the source file as bytes) and return ``&[u8]`` sliced at ``[range.start_byte(), range.end_byte())``; tree-sitter works on BYTE offsets (not character offsets), so the contract is byte-accurate, and the Python port keeps it byte-accurate (``src[self.range.start_byte() : self.range.end_byte()]`` returns ``bytes``; the caller ``.decode()`` for a ``str``). Fifth, **``NodeKind``'s tagged enum collapses to ONE frozen dataclass + ``NodeKindKind`` discriminator + four optional payload slots**: grok models ``NodeKind`` as a ``match``-able enum with four payload-carrying variants (``Scope(LocalScope)`` / ``Def(LocalDef)`` / ``Import(LocalImport)`` / ``Ref(Reference)``); Python has no enum-with-payload, so the port uses ONE dataclass (``kind: NodeKindKind`` discriminator + ``scope`` / ``definition`` / ``import_`` / ``reference`` four ``| None`` payload slots, defaulting to ``None``) -- exactly one payload is set per instance, an invariant enforced by the constructors and guarded by ``assert self.<payload> is not None`` in the dispatch methods. The payload field names dodge Python keywords: ``definition`` (not ``def``) and ``import_`` (trailing underscore, not ``import``); ``scope`` holds the ``LocalScope`` payload. This is the SAME tagged-union-collapse pattern R300 used for ``FileEvent``. Sixth, **``NodeKind::range`` vs ``NodeKind::identifier_range`` is the distinguishing dispatch case**: grok's ``range()`` returns the SCOPE range for ``Def`` (the def's full context, i.e. ``definition.scope.range``) but the identifier's own range for the other variants, while ``identifier_range()`` ALWAYS returns the identifier's own range; for ``Def`` this means ``range() != identifier_range()`` (the scope range vs the identifier range), and the Python port mirrors this exactly with two ``match`` statements that differ ONLY in the ``DEF`` arm (``range()`` returns ``self.definition.scope.range``; ``identifier_range()`` returns ``self.definition.range``). The ``match`` dispatch replaces grok's enum ``match``; each arm carries an ``assert self.<payload> is not None`` guard so a malformed ``NodeKind`` (payload missing for its kind) raises ``AssertionError`` rather than silently returning ``None``. Seventh, **``NodeKindKind`` is a Pythonic discriminator with NO grok counterpart**: grok needs no discriminator because the enum variant IS the discriminator; the Python port needs one because the tagged-union is collapsed to a dataclass, so ``NodeKindKind(Enum)`` (SCOPE / DEF / IMPORT / REF) is introduced -- its member VALUES mirror grok's variant names (``"Scope"`` / ``"Def"`` / etc.) for clarity, and it lives under the ``scope_graph`` subpackage barrel only (NOT re-exported at the crate root, because it has no grok counterpart to mirror). Eighth, **the crate-root barrel EXTENDS 9 -> 16 to mirror grok ``lib.rs`` re-exporting the 7 node symbols**: grok's crate root re-exports ``Symbol`` / ``SymbolId`` / ``LocalScope`` / ``LocalDef`` / ``LocalImport`` / ``Reference`` / ``NodeKind`` (but NOT ``EdgeKind``, which is only consumed inside ``scope_graph``); the Python port mirrors this -- the crate-root ``__init__.py`` grows from R300's 9 symbols to 16 (adding the 7 node symbols), while ``EdgeKind`` and the Pythonic ``NodeKindKind`` stay subpackage-only. This extension is a legitimate crate-root contract evolution that BROKE R300's over-strict ``set(crate_root.__all__) == set(types.__all__)`` equality assertion (the crate root is now a SUPERSET of the types barrel), fixed in-place by relaxing to a subset assertion (``set(types.__all__) <= set(crate_root.__all__)``) -- see Verification.
